$comment: Explicit exclusions from the derived corpus. The corpus itself is not listed anywhere:
it is every item English exists for in .source/ that at least one target locale already
holds a translation of. An entry here drops an item from that whatever is on disk, and
An exclusion binds on BOTH sides: the item stops counting towards completeness, and it
stops being validated and published. A translated file for it stays on disk, inert, and
comes back into scope the moment its entry is deleted.
An entry may narrow that to the item's BODY with "scope": "body". The item then stays in
the corpus for its translatable frontmatter (a title, a description): that copy is still
required, counted and published, while the Markdown body is none of the three and is never
published at all. "scope": "item" is the default and is the whole-item exclusion above.
scripts/lib/exclusions.mjs is the only reader of either.

not-yet-live exercise: TEMPORARY. This exercise is written in the front-end curriculum but is not part of the
course yet: it sits past the last shipped level, so no learner can reach it.
ITS TITLE AND DESCRIPTION ARE STILL TRANSLATED, in every locale. They are card copy: two
short strings that surface in listings and on level pages, where an English title in an
otherwise translated list is a visible hole. So the exercise's instructions are excluded
with "scope": "body" (frontmatter required, body not), and its message catalog, which is
all insides, is excluded whole. Nothing about the exercise's TEACHING content is expected:
not the instruction body, the scenarios, the tasks, the hints, the checks or the function
descriptions. That is the expensive half, and deferring it is the whole point.
A body-excluded instruction page is never published. Its translated title and description
reach the merged curriculum catalog; its prose artifact and its index entry are not written
at all, because a page with a Hungarian title over an English body is worse for a learner
than a page that is not there.
WHEN THE EXERCISE GOES LIVE, DELETE ITS LINES HERE, in the same change that adds it to the
course. Its body and its catalog are invisible to completeness until then, so a live one
left listed here would let a locale be declared complete while that exercise renders
untranslated (a catalog has no English fallback: a learner sees raw key names). That is the
risk this trades against, deliberately, and only for as long as the exercise is unreachable.
The live set is the 'Stage 3 exercise queue' in the translator repo's orchestrator.md,
which is every exercise up to and including exercise/formal-dinner. It is the source of
truth and is deliberately not copied here: these entries are the complement of it, so
this list is what needs regenerating when that queue moves, and nothing else.
unshipped interpreter language: TEMPORARY. Jiki is launching JAVASCRIPT-FIRST. The front-end curriculum's AGENTS.md says so
in as many words: we ship JavaScript, and Python and Jikiscript support come later. The
interpreters for those two languages exist in the source repo and carry a full English
message catalog, but no learner can select either language, so nothing in either catalog
can reach a screen.
That makes them the same category as a not-yet-live exercise: English nobody is expected to
translate yet. Unlike an exercise there is no card copy to keep, because an interpreter
catalog is ALL INSIDES: runtime and syntax error messages, and nothing a listing renders. So
the exclusion is the whole item, with no "scope", which is the default.
The javascript catalog is NOT here and must never be. It is the shipped language, it is what
every production locale already translates, and it is the one interpreter whose messages a
learner sees today.
WHEN A LANGUAGE SHIPS, DELETE ITS LINE HERE, in the same change that makes it selectable.
Until then its catalog is invisible to completeness, so a shipped language left listed here
would let a locale be declared complete while every error that interpreter raises renders as
a raw key path (the interpreter runtime sets fallbackLng: false on purpose, so there is no
English to fall back to). That is the risk this trades against, deliberately, and only for as
long as the language is unreachable.
The source of truth for which languages are shipped is the front-end, not this file: the
curriculum's JavaScript-first note and the language a lesson can actually be opened in.
These entries are the complement of that, so this list is what needs revisiting when it moves.
